newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen capped by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen capped by profit-taking.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to be capped by profit-taking pressures on Friday after the key market index was lifted by active buying in the high-tech sector over the past two days, brokers said.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 160.51 points or 0.79 percent to close at 20,519.25. September futures closed 120 points higher at 20,550.

"Given New York's correction overnight and the three-day weekend, the Nikkei 225 is likely to see profit-taking," said a general manager at a second-tier securities house. Tokyo markets will be closed Monday as Sunday is a national holiday.
On Thursday, Wall Street stocks paused after their record runs, with the Dow industrials falling 18.11 points to end at 8,020.77 and the Nasdaq composite off 11.78 points at 1,568.85.

"I expect the Tokyo market will keep a firm tone, but the Nikkei 225 may hover for a while, since heavy profit-taking is expected between 20,500 and 21,000," said a broker at another second-tier securities house.

Many brokers also expect to see a slow start to individual stock options trade, which will begins on the Tokyo and Osaka bourses on Friday. They said the derivatives market would have little affect on cash stock trading on Friday.
Wall Street's record-setting run, which had cheered the key Nikkei index recently, slipped back on Thursday and this also created caution in Tokyo, brokers said.
On Thursday, the Dow industrials fell 18.11 points to end at 8,020.77 and the Nasdaq composite was off 11.78 points at 1,568.85.
On the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, turnover dwindled to 192 million shares by midday from 263 million shares traded by Thursday midday.
Gainers slightly outnumbered losers 508 to 490, while 229 issues were unchanged.
The broader-based TOPIX index was up 0.50 point or 0.03 percent to 1,553.64. The Nikkei 300 average stood 0.06 point or 0.02 percent higher at 302.79.

Some blue-chip shares, such as Sony Corp, resumed their upward trend, backed by the the yen's weakness against the dollar. Sony's shares hit a record high of 10,900 yen by midday, up 200 yen from Thursday's close.

Shares in Nikko Securities Co were well-bid in heavy trade, helped by news that the Japanese brokerage will set up a joint investment consulting firm in Japan with Smith Barney International Inc of the United States.
Nikko's shares rose 15 yen to end the morning at 740 yen, in a turnover of 3.636 million shares, the second-largest volume on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd's shares slipped after surging recently on the news that the bank and Swiss Bank Corp would form a global strategic alliance. LTCB's shares were down 24 yen at 551 yen.
By sector, gainers were credit/lease, miscellaneous manufacturing, railway/bus, food and insurers. The major decliners were cars, air transport and land transport.
